title: `QUANTILE_CONT`: `lo·(1−d) + hi·d` in doubles, NaN between -inf and +inf
verdict: between the neighbours up to rounding; NaN between -inf and +inf; the written SQL clamps
description: `QUANTILE_CONT(x, q)` of `n` values computes `RN = (n − 1)·q` in doubles, takes the values `lo` and `hi` at positions `⌊RN⌋` and `⌈RN⌉` in order, and gives `lo` where they are one position, else `lo·(1 − d) + hi·d` with `d = RN − ⌊RN⌋`. Integers are cast to DOUBLE first and the result is a DOUBLE; DECIMAL gives a DECIMAL and DATE a TIMESTAMP, each interpolated in its own type; FLOAT stays FLOAT. `MEDIAN` of a number is `QUANTILE_CONT(x, 0.5)`.

The interpolation rounds: of neighbours that are equal it can give a double an ulp away from them, so the result can lie just outside [lo, hi]. Between -inf and +inf it is NaN (`-inf·(1 − d) + inf·d`); next to a NaN it is NaN. Large neighbours do not overflow (`-1.5e308` and `1.5e308` give `0.0`), since each is scaled before the sum. Since `RN` is a double, a fraction such as `0.1` may land just off a whole position; the result then differs from the exact one by rounding only.
reference: `AggFn.quantile true num scale` (`contValue`, #53): for the exact `q = num / 10^scale`, the doubles at positions `⌊(n−1)·q⌋` and `⌈(n−1)·q⌉` in order; the one value where they coincide, else DuckDB's `lo·(1 − d) + hi·d` kept between `lo` and `hi` (`interpolate`). The reference allows any double between the two neighbours (`contAllowed`, `AggFn.Allowed`), so contracts know the result lies within the argument's range. Integers are converted to doubles first; DECIMAL, DATE and TIMESTAMP arguments are refused.

DuckDB differs from the reference only where its rounding leaves [lo, hi], and between -inf and +inf (NaN, where the reference keeps +inf). The DuckDB writer clamps its `QUANTILE_CONT` to `[MIN(x), MAX(x)]`, which gives the model's +inf there.
